_comment: MLPR's own aircraft-type-to-icon table. Hand-authored by this project, NOT a redistribution of any external ICAO/tar1090/BaseStation type database -- see CLAUDE.md's icon classification section for why. 'exact' always wins over 'prefix'; prefixes are tried longest-first and must be at least 3 characters (a 2-char prefix is never safe -- see the collision notes below). This is Stage 1/2's illustrative minimal table (~25-30 of the most common types); Stage 3 expands it to full coverage.
_collisionNotes: Before adding any prefix, check it doesn't also match a type in a different icon category. Known traps: 'A3' catches both A30B/A306/A310 (widebody2) AND A318-A321 (narrowbody) -- split into 'A31'-family exacts plus separate 'A32'/'A33'/'A34'/'A35'/'A38' prefixes, never a bare 'A3'. 'C1' catches both C130/C160/C17 (military transports) AND C152/C172/C182/C206/C208 (Cessna singles) -- never used, both families are exact-only or use a longer, safe prefix. 'B7' catches both B73x (narrowbody) AND B74x/B76x/B77x/B78x (widebody) -- only used at 3 chars (B73/B74/B76/B77/B78), never as bare 'B7'.

military._comment: Consulted ONLY when the aircraft's dbFlags military bit is set, and ONLY for type designators that are genuinely ambiguous between a civilian and a government/military airframe using the SAME type code. These two entries are illustrative placeholders (A330/747 airframes are sometimes reused as tankers/AWACS-derivatives under their base civilian type code in some databases) -- verify against real data (Stage 4's tools/ script, plus manual spot-checking) before trusting them.
